page: The Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by AWS Graviton3 processors built on ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture. The instance delivers 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with one thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, includes hardware AES acceleration, and does not include GPU resources.

A key hardware component of the m7gd.2xlarge is the inclusion of 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 4 Gbps baseline network link. In benchmark testing, the memory subsystem demonstrated strong throughput, achieving a PassMark memory score of 2,917.64 and uncached read-only memory bandwidth of 157.33 GB/sec. General compute results were balanced, including 12,240.79 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,982.0. In-memory data store performance showed 13.58 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads, with static web serving reaching 15.88 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge under compute-intensive compression and LLM inference scenarios. The instance showed weak performance in bzip3 decompression, reaching 7.39 GB/sec single-threaded, and a PassMark CPU score of 6,064.33. Prompt processing on a 7B LLM model remained low at 14.11 tokens per second due to the lack of specialized matrix coprocessors or discrete acceleration. From a resource efficiency standpoint, the Graviton3 architecture provides dedicated physical cores and local NVMe capacity without the hyperthreading contention common in shared x86 configurations.

The Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is suitable for general-purpose application hosting, high-throughput web serving, caching tiers, containerized microservices, and databases that require low-latency scratch storage on direct-attached NVMe disks.
description: The Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated ARM64 cores powered by AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processors at 2.6 GHz. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and incorporates 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage with a 4 Gbps baseline network connection. The platform lacks discrete GPUs and x86 vector extensions, relying on Nitro virtualization and hardware AES support. Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput with a PassMark memory score of 2,917.64, alongside consistent general-purpose compute metrics, such as a multi-core Geekbench score of 7,982.0 and 13.58 million Redis SET operations per second. Complex compression and large-scale language model prompt evaluation show weaker efficiency. The instance delivers resource density and fast local I/O for workloads such as container platforms, relational databases, cache nodes, and web serving fleets.
